report.source_text: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination showed normal intracranial pressure and his CSF was a crystalline fluid with 2 leukocytes/uL, containing 6.11 mmol/L of glucose (Reference Range: 2.5–4.5). His CSF contained 0.63 g/L of protein (Reference Range: 0.15–0.45). The IgG index of the CSF was elevated at 4.13 (Reference Range: < 0.85). Oligoclonal bands (Type III) (HYDRAGEL 3 & 9 ISOFOCUSING gel) were found in the CSF. Antibodies in the CSF for cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus and herpes simplex virus were all negative. No infectious pathogens were identified in the blood or in the CSF.

report.source_text: Extensive laboratory investigation showed an only slightly elevated white blood cell count (11.6 × 10^9 /L, Reference Range: 3.5–9.5), C-reactive protein level (10 mg/L, Reference Range: 0–8), and positive for antinuclear antibodies (1:1000, negative < 1:100). Serum sodium concentration, anti-dsDNA and ENA antibodies, ANCA and RF were all in the normal ranges. The tumor markers were unremarkable.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 85-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes presented with progressive lower limb weakness and urinary retention, rapidly progressing to delirium and coma. Initial neurological exam showed paraplegia without sensory or vision disturbance. Brain MRI on admission revealed focal symmetrical bilateral lesions in the thalamus with hyperintense T2 and FLAIR. CSF analysis showed normal intracranial pressure, minimal leukocytes (2/uL), elevated glucose (6.11 mmol/L), elevated protein (0.63 g/L), elevated IgG index (4.13), and Type III oligoclonal bands, with no infectious pathogens identified in CSF or blood. Extensive laboratory tests showed slightly elevated WBC and CRP, and positive antinuclear antibodies (1:1000), but negative for specific autoimmune and paraneoplastic antibodies (including AQP4 and MOG). A follow-up head MRI after 17 days showed enlargement of the bilateral thalamic lesions, low density changes on CT, slightly high intensity on DWI, and new progressive multiple lesions in the subcortical white matter, brain stem, and a hyperintense long segment of T2 in the thoracic spinal cord. The patient was treated with IV immunoglobulin (IVIG) but remained unconscious. Intravenous methylprednisolone was not administered due to age and diabetes. He developed pneumonia and passed away 38 days after onset from respiratory failure.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute neurological deficits including progressive lower limb weakness, urinary retention, delirium, and coma.
Brain MRI on admission demonstrated focal symmetrical bilateral lesions in the thalamus with hyperintense T2 and FLAIR.
CSF examination showed signs of inflammation (elevated protein, elevated IgG index, Type III oligoclonal bands) but minimal pleocytosis (2 leukocytes/uL) and no infectious pathogens.
Follow-up MRI after 17 days showed enlargement of bilateral thalamic lesions and new progressive multiple lesions in the subcortical white matter, brain stem, and thoracic spinal cord.
Specific antibodies for demyelinating diseases (anti-AQP4, anti-MOG) and paraneoplastic syndromes were negative in blood and CSF.
The patient's condition progressed despite IVIG treatment, leading to death from respiratory failure 38 days after onset.
